Safe Work Environment Description: Explore whether the company prioritizes physical safety with consistent practices and whether leadership actively addresses organizational risks that can affect well-being (e.g., harassment, excessive overtime, overload, high turnover, training gaps, or lack of work control).
Safe Work Environment Action 1: Implement daily safety routine by shift (brief talk + risk checklist).
Safe Work Environment Action 2: Activate anti-harassment protocol with confidential channel, investigation and clear sanctions.
Safe Work Environment Action 3: Diagnosis of workloads and overtime by line/area and phased reduction plan.
Safe Work Environment Action 4: Establish psychosocial risk committee with quarterly goals and visible monitoring.
Job Security Description: Measures perception of employment stability and confidence in permanence, associated with company practices to maintain stability and reduce turnover.
Job Security Action 1: Communicate a stability plan (demand projections, hiring/adjustment criteria).
Job Security Action 2: Design retention strategy for critical roles (permanence bonuses/internal mobility).
Job Security Action 3: Train managers in trust-based leadership and communication of operational certainty.
Job Security Action 4: Conduct exit interviews and "stay interviews" with root cause actions.
Fair Compensation Description: Evaluates whether employees perceive that salary and benefits are equitable and competitive compared to what the industry offers.
Fair Compensation Action 1: Execute salary benchmark against industry and region.
Fair Compensation Action 2: Fix gaps with band adjustments and internal equity.
Fair Compensation Action 3: Clarify compensation structure and benefits through clear communication.
Fair Compensation Action 4: Link incentives to safety, quality and productivity with simple rules.
Open Communication Description: Reviews transparency and frequency of communication on relevant business and quality topics, and also perception of fair treatment by key leadership figures (plant manager, production, HR, supervisor and team leader).
Open Communication Action 1: Implement weekly briefing by area/shift with goals, changes and priorities.
Open Communication Action 2: Establish monthly plant communication calendar (results, quality, safety).
Open Communication Action 3: Train leaders in fair treatment and respectful communication with 180/360 evaluation.
Open Communication Action 4: Create Q&A channel with defined response times.
Employee Participation Description: Determines if employees are invited to participate in decisions affecting their work, if their input is valued in operational and safety improvements, and if they are involved in process/standards update initiatives.
Employee Participation Action 1: Activate improvement circles by cell/line with bi-weekly meetings.
Employee Participation Action 2: Implement ideas system with mandatory feedback.
Employee Participation Action 3: Include operational representatives in standards and process updates.
Employee Participation Action 4: Publicly recognize improvements implemented by teams.
Recognition and Reward Description: Measures perception of regular recognition for quality and operational contributions, and existence of rewards for reliable performance (e.g., assignments to critical roles).
Recognition and Reward Action 1: Launch immediate recognition program for safety, quality and attendance.
Recognition and Reward Action 2: Define transparent criteria for critical role assignments and rewards.
Recognition and Reward Action 3: Train managers in micro-recognition and specific positive feedback.
Recognition and Reward Action 4: Publish monthly achievements board by team/shift.
Training and Development Description: Evaluates whether training is sufficient and continuous beyond induction, and whether the company provides trainers and resources to develop key job skills.
Training and Development Action 1: Develop skills matrix by position and gaps by team.
Training and Development Action 2: Implement annual training plan by shift with guaranteed minimum hours.
Training and Development Action 3: Certify internal trainers and ensure practical materials/resources.
Training and Development Action 4: Evaluate effectiveness with competency tests and rework/incident metrics.
Work-Life Balance Description: Reviews whether shift patterns and overtime are reasonable and whether absenteeism and time-off policies are managed respectfully.
Work-Life Balance Action 1: Redefine overtime rules with equitable rotation and limits per period.
Work-Life Balance Action 2: Adjust shift patterns to reduce fatigue (planned breaks and rotations).
Work-Life Balance Action 3: Establish clear and humane process for absenteeism and time off.
Work-Life Balance Action 4: Monitor well-being with pulse surveys and safety metrics.
Professional Advancement Description: Explores whether there are clear growth paths based on skills and performance and whether the organization invests in preparing employees for higher roles (e.g., team leaders or skilled positions).
Professional Advancement Action 1: Create and communicate career paths by job family.
Professional Advancement Action 2: Define promotion criteria based on verifiable skills and performance.
Professional Advancement Action 4: Post vacancies internally first and measure internal mobility.
Employee Support Description: Evaluates availability of accessible support resources (such as counseling or assistance programs) to address personal and work-related challenges related to stress, absenteeism or turnover.
Employee Support Action 1: Implement or strengthen an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
Employee Support Action 2: Spread clear access to counseling, emotional support and guidance.
Employee Support Action 3: Train leaders for early detection of stress and referral.
Employee Support Action 4: Integrate periodic wellness and stress management campaigns.
Safe Work Environment Strength: Consistent practices and leadership that manages psychosocial and operational risks.
Safe Work Environment Weakness: Prevention of workplace violence, overload or uncontrolled overtime.
Safe Work Environment Opportunity: Align NOM-035 programs with internal audits and preventive leadership.
Safe Work Environment Threat: Accidents, sanctions, climate deterioration and operational stoppages.
Job Security Strength: Perception of stability and visible efforts against turnover.
Job Security Weakness: Employment uncertainty that affects commitment and performance.
Job Security Opportunity: Retention strategies and business direction communication.
Fair Compensation Weakness: Inequity or wage lag that fuels turnover.
Fair Compensation Opportunity: Salary range review and flexible benefits.
Open Communication Strength: Regular communication and fair treatment from key leaders.
Open Communication Weakness: Rumors, perceived favoritism, low hierarchical credibility.
Employee Participation Strength: Real involvement in decisions and improvements.
Employee Participation Weakness: Personnel disconnection and resistance to change.
Employee Participation Threat: Cynical culture if contributions are not implemented.
Recognition and Reward Strength: Frequent recognition and rewards for reliability.
Recognition and Reward Weakness: Effort not valued and perception of arbitrariness.
Professional Advancement Strength: Clear paths and investment in development.
Professional Advancement Weakness: Stagnation and dependence on external hiring.
